prompt: How does the section define the mechanism of a reaction?

choices.text: The series of steps leading from starting materials to products
The balanced equation for the overall reaction
choices.why: The balanced equation shows only where the reaction starts and ends. The mechanism is the series of steps in between.

choices.text: The rate law measured for the overall reaction
choices.why: A rate law describes how fast the reaction goes. The mechanism is the sequence of steps that carries the starting materials to the products.

choices.text: The slowest single step in the reaction
choices.why: One step is only part of the mechanism. The mechanism is the whole series of steps from starting materials to products.

explanation: The section defines a mechanism as a series of steps leading from the starting materials to the products. Each step is a simple reaction, and together they make up the overall reaction.

prompt: What does the section call the simple steps that make up a reaction mechanism?

choices.why: Intermediates are the species formed after each step, not the steps themselves. The steps are elementary reactions.
The overall reaction is what the steps add up to. Each simple step is an elementary reaction.
A side reaction leads somewhere other than the products. The steps on the path to the products are elementary reactions.

explanation: The section calls the simple steps of a mechanism elementary reactions. An overall reaction is composed of a series of them.

prompt: According to the section, what is formed after each step of a mechanism, on the way to the products?

choices.why: Starting materials are what the mechanism begins with, not what the steps make. Each step forms an intermediate.
The section says nothing about catalysts here. What each step forms is an intermediate, which the next step uses.
There is only one overall reaction, made of all the steps. Each step forms an intermediate.

explanation: After each step of the mechanism an intermediate is formed. It quickly undergoes another step, forming the next intermediate, until the products are reached.

prompt: Why does the section say an intermediate is short-lived?

choices.text: It escapes from the reaction mixture
choices.why: An intermediate isn't lost from the mixture. It is used up because it quickly reacts in the next step.

choices.text: It turns back into starting material
choices.why: The section has an intermediate go forward, quickly undergoing another step to form the next intermediate.

choices.text: It is formed only at the very end
choices.why: Intermediates are formed along the way, after each step. They are short-lived because the next step uses them quickly.

explanation: An intermediate is short-lived because it quickly undergoes another step to form the next intermediate. That is why intermediates don't build up the way products do.

prompt: What does the section say about how the rate of an overall reaction relates to its elementary reactions?

choices.text: It depends in some way on their rates
It is independent of their rates
choices.why: The overall reaction is made of the elementary reactions, so its rate must depend on theirs. The section says it is somehow dependent on them.

choices.text: It is always the sum of their rates
choices.why: The section doesn't give a simple sum. It says only that the overall rate somehow depends on the rates of the steps, and asks how.

choices.text: It always equals the rate of the first step
choices.why: The section doesn't single out the first step. It says the overall rate depends in some way on the rates of the steps.

explanation: Because an overall reaction is composed of a series of elementary reactions, its rate is somehow dependent on the rates of those smaller reactions. Working out how is the question the section raises.

prompt: A proposed mechanism has the steps X + Y → I and I + Z → P. Which species is the intermediate?

choices.why: P is formed in the last step and not used again, so it is the product. I is formed in step 1 and used up in step 2.
Y is a starting material, present before any step. The intermediate is I, formed by step 1 and used by step 2.
Z is a starting material that enters in step 2. The intermediate is I, which step 1 makes and step 2 uses.

explanation: I is formed after the first step and quickly undergoes the second step to give P. X, Y and Z are starting materials and P is the product.

prompt: A proposed mechanism for the decomposition of ozone has the steps O_3 → O_2 + O and O + O_3 → 2O_2. Which species is the intermediate?

choices.why: O_2 is formed in both steps and never used up, so it is a product. O is formed in step 1 and used up in step 2.
O_3 is the starting material; it is used in both steps but never formed. O is the short-lived species in between.
O is formed in step 1 and consumed in step 2, so it is an intermediate. Every step but the last forms one.

explanation: O is formed after the first step and quickly undergoes the second step. O_3 is the starting material and O_2 the product, so O is the intermediate.

prompt: The two elementary reactions O_3 → O_2 + O and O + O_3 → 2O_2 make up a mechanism. What overall reaction do they make up?

choices.why: This is the sum of the steps before cancelling. O is formed in step 1 and used in step 2, so it drops out.
That is only the first step. The overall reaction includes the second step too, which uses up O.
This isn't balanced: it has 3 O atoms on the left and 6 on the right. Both steps use one O_3, so 2O_3 → 3O_2.

explanation: Adding the steps gives 2O_3 + O → 3O_2 + O, and the intermediate O cancels, leaving 2O_3 → 3O_2. The overall reaction is composed of the series of elementary reactions, with the intermediates removed.

prompt: In the overall reaction made up by a two-step mechanism, which kind of species does not appear?

choices.why: The starting materials are where the overall reaction begins, so they are on its left side. The intermediate is formed and used up, so it cancels.
The products are where the overall reaction ends, so they are on its right side. It is the intermediate that cancels.
Step 1 includes starting materials, which stay in the overall reaction. Only the intermediate, formed in one step and used in the next, cancels.

explanation: An intermediate is formed in one step and used up in the next, so it appears on both sides when the steps are added and cancels out. The overall reaction shows only the starting materials and products.

prompt: In a two-step mechanism, what does the second step use that the first step made?

choices.why: The product is what the mechanism ends with; no later step uses it. The second step uses the intermediate from the first.
The first step uses starting material; it doesn't make more. What step 1 makes and step 2 uses is the intermediate.
The steps form a series: the intermediate made in step 1 quickly undergoes step 2. They are linked, not independent.

explanation: The intermediate formed after the first step quickly undergoes the next step. That link is what makes the steps a series leading from starting materials to products.

prompt: In a reaction mixture, species Q is formed in one step and then stays in the mixture at the end, unchanged. Why is Q not an intermediate?

choices.text: No later step uses it up
It was formed in a step
choices.why: Intermediates are formed in steps too. What makes Q a product is that no later step uses it.

choices.text: It is present at the start
choices.why: Q was formed during the reaction, so it isn't a starting material. It isn't an intermediate because nothing uses it up.

choices.text: Intermediates form only in the last step
choices.why: It is the other way round: an intermediate is formed after a step and used by a later step. Whatever the last step forms is a product.

explanation: An intermediate is short-lived because it quickly undergoes another step. A species that is formed and then remains unchanged at the end is a product.

prompt: A mechanism has three steps: A → I_1, I_1 → I_2 and I_2 → P. How many different intermediates does it have?
explanation: I_1 is formed in step 1 and used in step 2, and I_2 is formed in step 2 and used in step 3, so there are 2 intermediates. The last step forms P, the product, which nothing uses.

prompt: A mechanism leads from A to the product P through the intermediates I_1, I_2 and I_3, one after another. Each elementary reaction turns one species into the next. How many elementary reactions does the mechanism have?
explanation: The steps are A → I_1, I_1 → I_2, I_2 → I_3 and I_3 → P, so there are 4 elementary reactions. Each step but the last forms an intermediate, so three intermediates need four steps.

prompt: Which statement about an overall reaction and its elementary reactions matches the section?

choices.text: The overall reaction is composed of a series of elementary reactions
Each elementary reaction is composed of overall reactions
choices.why: This turns the relationship around. Elementary reactions are the simple steps; the overall reaction is made of a series of them.

choices.text: An overall reaction always happens in a single step
choices.why: The section describes an overall reaction as a series of steps, each forming an intermediate. It need not be one step.

choices.text: Elementary reactions occur only after the overall reaction
choices.why: The elementary reactions are the overall reaction, carried out step by step. They don't come after it.

explanation: The mechanism is a series of simple steps, the elementary reactions, and the overall reaction is composed of them. That is why its rate depends on the rates of those smaller reactions.

prompt: A balanced equation shows only reactants R and products S. Why might a chemist still look for intermediates?

choices.text: The reaction may go through several steps not shown
Intermediates must appear in balanced equations
choices.why: Intermediates cancel when the steps are added, so they don't appear in the overall equation. That is why they can be hidden.
Products are where the mechanism ends; nothing uses them up. Intermediates are the short-lived species between the steps.

choices.text: Intermediates are long-lived and easy to see
choices.why: The section says intermediates are short-lived, because each quickly undergoes another step.

explanation: An overall reaction can be composed of a series of elementary reactions, with a short-lived intermediate after each step. Those intermediates cancel from the overall equation, so the equation alone doesn't show the mechanism.
